prose_updates.tldr: Changing pathogen variants make early-versus-late vaccine challenge risk depend on one latent coupling of exposures and responses across periods. The response type permits a noninfecting period-one exposure to alter later controlled susceptibility, and a disclosed \(\delta\in[0,1]\) bounds the altered fraction. Pointwise in \(\delta\), a finite common-history polytope exactly represents every compatible law, its extended reference-mixture ratio set is sharp, reciprocal endpoints are attained under the separate denominator condition, and a common-law dual certifies strict signs. For \(K=2\), finitely many linear programs recover the exact affine hull of the positive comparison face, and a quadratic cross-product test is necessary and sufficient for the Perényi--Stensrud controlled-risk contrast to be constant and equal its observed-hazard counterpart; empty, nonconstant, and constant-mismatch cases have explicit certificates. Exact multinomial inversion, with \(\Gamma_0(u;\gamma)=\Delta\), gives unconditional whole-set coverage after projection through every nonempty fiber and through the prespecified \(\delta\)-envelope, without independence across sampling blocks or a conditional-on-realized-arm-sizes claim.

project_justification.fill: The substantive chain supplies, pointwise in \(\delta\), exact common-history compression, an always-defined extended sharp set, finite attained reciprocal endpoints under the disclosed denominator condition, and a common-law sign dual with compatible counterlaws. For \(K=2\), the collapse boundary is computed by a positive-face linear program, linear programs for the exact affine hull, and a quadratic identity test; its failures yield an infeasibility certificate, two compatible laws with different controlled-risk contrasts, or one compatible-law observable-mismatch witness. Exact primitive-cell multinomial inversion defines \(\Gamma_0(u;\gamma)=\Delta\) at zero total count and projects the simultaneous primitive confidence event through every nonempty fixed-\(\delta\) fiber and the prespecified sensitivity envelope, yielding unconditional whole-set coverage. Case-frequency substitution and the fixed-fiber policy-mixture radius remain separate questions.

sampling_model.units: For each trial arm, conditional on that arm's own realized total, the mutually exclusive categories consisting of no first infection and first infection by period and variant have the stated multinomial law. For each period-specific external total, exposure counts on \(\mathcal V_0\) have the stated multinomial law. No independence among the two trial-arm blocks and two external-period blocks is required: each block's exact error bound is first averaged over its own possibly random total, and a union bound gives simultaneous coverage unconditionally over the trial and external samples. No joint conditional coverage claim given the realized trial arm sizes is made.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The trial and exposure cell probabilities are covered by exact likelihood-ratio-ordered multinomial inversions at Bonferroni level \(\alpha/4\) for each of two arms and two periods. At total count zero, \(T_p(0)=0\) and \(\Gamma_0(u;\gamma)=\Delta\), so zero-total and zero-cell samples require no correction. The simultaneous primitive confidence set is projected through every nonempty \(\mathcal P_\delta(b',q',\omega)\) fiber; the same primitive event covers the union over the prespecified \(\mathcal D\). The construction does not studentize or select an endpoint optimizer.

prose_updates.related_work: Janvin and Stensrud (2025, Theorem 1 and Appendix B) establish sharp finite single-pathogen two-period challenge-effect bounds and attaining laws; their multiple-version analysis does not retain external period-specific variant margins or index later controlled response by a prior noninfecting exposure. Perényi and Stensrud (2025, Section 5 and the marginal \(CSE_k\) identification proposition) identify a time-to-event challenge subtype effect from observed cause-specific hazards under time-to-event exchangeability, positivity, consistency, exposure necessity, no cross-infectivity, a covariate-invariant exposure ratio, and scaled-new-infection proportionality. Here their controlled-risk coordinates are represented by \(\rho_{ta}(x,e^{(v)})\), with the period-two coordinate based on \(R^{[0]}_{2av}\); instead of asserting class inclusion, the exact boundary is the vanishing of a computable quadratic cross-product on the LP-computed affine hull of the positive common-history face. Tomer and Biccler (2022) analyze temporal movement under specified competing-variant mechanisms. Follmann and Huang (2018), Gilbert et al. (2001), Edlefsen (2014), and van der Laan and Gilbert (2023) motivate why selected infecting strains require extra exposure and susceptibility restrictions, so case frequencies are not substituted for the external margins \(q\). Balke and Pearl (1997) inform the finite response-type lift. Romano and Shaikh (2010) and Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019) inform whole-set projection; the present construction uses exact multinomial inversion including the zero-total definition \(\Gamma_0(u;\gamma)=\Delta\), obtains simultaneous coverage by a union bound without block independence, and projects the resulting event through all nonempty fibers and the prespecified sensitivity envelope.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Exact common-history projection, the unconditional extended sharp set, finite attained reciprocal endpoints under the separately disclosed fiber-wide denominator condition, and common-history sign separation are substantive claims pointwise in prespecified \(\delta\). The target period-two risk uses \(R^{[0]}_{21v}\), while observed period-two infections use \(R^{[H_1]}_{2av}\); their discrepancy among noninfected exposees is bounded, not suppressed. For \(K=2\), collapse to the observed hazard contrast holds exactly when observed positivity and positive controlled-risk-face feasibility hold, the quadratic cross-product vanishes on the exact affine hull, and its constant equals the observed value. Failure of observed positivity makes that comparison undefined and is not an empty-face certificate. The exact multinomial confidence projection covers the full sharp fixed-\(\delta\) set, and the same unconditional event covers its prespecified \(\mathcal D\)-envelope; it makes no conditional coverage claim given realized arm sizes and uses no independence among count blocks. Fiber infeasibility is failure and never vacuous positivity. External exposure margins remain primitives; pooled case-strain frequencies do not replace them.

statement_notes.justification: The adjacent point-identification result now enters the external-margin analysis through an exact, finite collapse test rather than an asserted class inclusion.
statement_notes.gap: The result characterizes the boundary left open by replacing covariate-invariant exposure-ratio and scaled-new-infection restrictions with external exposure margins and a common-history sensitivity fiber: feasibility is linear-programmable, constancy is a quadratic identity on the exact affine hull, and equality to the observed contrast is a separate scalar check.
statement_notes.consumer: Vaccine researchers can certify collapse, distinguish an undefined observed comparison from an infeasible controlled-risk face, or output compatible full-law witnesses for nonconstancy and observable mismatch.
